subject: Save Meta Data Only from Part 1

messages.author: c4bb1002428326c2
messages.subject: Save Meta Data Only from Part 1
parts:
Hello, 

Is it possible to save only `metashort` data from executing part 1 of `g.shell.GGIR`? My goal is to process a couple hundred `.bin` files from GENEA devices, saving only the .RData file produced after processing.

Thanks,
Michael

messages.author: 5270e62a7d3ec577
messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Save Meta Data Only from Part 1
parts:
Hi Michael, simply stating "mode=c(1)" withing the shell function will do this and generate the part 1 meta files only.

Kind regards,
Ben

kind regards,
Ben

messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Save Meta Data Only from Part 1
parts:
Thanks for the response, Ben. To give more detail, I am running `g.shell.GGIR` with `mode = 1` already chosen. However, this produces a new folder in a specified directory with the .RData file. Then, I have to load the .RData file, which loads in lists `C`, `I`, and `M`, but I am only interested in `M$metashort`. So, my goal is to collect all `M$metashort` files in one folder, discarding everything else.

Of course, I can do a few steps afterwards to get just the `metashort` files all in one location; but it would be nice to avoid this. An ideal workflow would be:
1. Run g.shell.GGIR (mode 1) on .bin file
2. Save `M$metashort` to a folder, discarding all else
3. Repeat over all `.bin` files
End result: one folder accumulated with only `M$metashort` files

Thanks,
Michael

messages.author: 5270e62a7d3ec577
messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Save Meta Data Only from Part 1
parts:
Hi Michael,

I'm not aware of an existing way to do this, unless you edited the function within the shell function. Someone else may chip in and prove me wrong.

A script to do this across all files in a directory would be a really simple solution though. If it's only a few hundred files this would barely take any time at all to read in, drop unwanted data and save just the meta short in a separate output folder. This is what I would do for a quick win.

If I were in your position though I would share your ambition to do it all in the one step! Maybe someone else will know of a cleaner way of doing this :)

Kind regards,
Ben

kind regards,
Ben

Hi Michael,

I saw you had no other replies yet, so I just had 5 minutes to check this more thoroughly. I don't know how proficient you are with R and Github, but it seems at face value like you could easily implement this as an output straight after line line 550 here: https://github.com/wadpac/GGIR/blob/master/R/g.part1.R  

You could compile your own version with the code changes on a local pc, better yet you could follow-up with a pull request on github so anyone else wanting to extract metashort files will benefit :)

Ben

messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Save Meta Data Only from Part 1
parts:
Hi Michael,

Did you consider argument "epochvalues2csv=TRUE", which exports the basic time series data to a csv-file? If you do not want imputation, use argument do.imp=FALSE.

I did not implement this in GGIR part1, because I wanted the option to impute missing values, which takes place in part 2.

Cheers,
Vincent
